Q: What happens to the legal enforceability of a digitally signed contract under this rule?
A: Provided it meets the requirements of section 63, the digitally signed contract has the exact same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as a physically signed paper contract. [Source: Section 61, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 62: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

Q: Which specific section dictates how the contents of an electronic record should be proved?
A: The contents of electronic records may be proved in accordance with the provisions of section 63. [Source: Section 62, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 62: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

Q: What does Section 62 of BSA 2023 state about electronic records?
A: Section 62 of BSA 2023 states that the contents of electronic records may be proved in accordance with the provisions of section 63. [Source: Section 62, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 62: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

Q: If a prosecutor wants to prove the contents of a hard drive, where in the BSA should they look for the specific procedure?
A: They must look to the provisions of section 63, as directed by Section 62. [Source: Section 62, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 62: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

Q: What specific part of an electronic record does this section address proving?
A: This section specifically addresses proving the 'contents' of electronic records. [Source: Section 62, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 62: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

Q: Are there separate, different rules for proving the contents of different types of electronic records under this section?
A: No, the section broadly refers 'electronic records' to be proved in accordance with section 63, without internal exceptions. [Source: Section 62, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 62: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

Q: What happens if a party ignores Section 63 when trying to prove an electronic record's contents?
A: The evidence will likely be inadmissible because Section 62 explicitly directs that the proof be in accordance with Section 63. [Source: Section 62, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 63: Admissibility of electronic records

Q: Can a printout of an electronic record be treated as a document and admitted as evidence without the original computer?
A: Yes, any information in an electronic record printed on paper (computer output) shall be deemed a document and admissible without the original, if specific conditions relating to the computer's regular use and proper operation are satisfied. [Source: Section 63, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admissibility of electronic records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 63: Admissibility of electronic records

Q: What does Section 63 of BSA 2023 establish regarding computer outputs?
A: Section 63 of BSA 2023 establishes that computer outputs are deemed documents and are admissible as evidence of their contents, provided strict conditions about the computer's regular use, data feeding, and a certificate are met. [Source: Section 63, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admissibility of electronic records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 63: Admissibility of electronic records

Q: If a company regularly backs up its sales data to a server, and a printout of a specific month's sales is submitted to court with a signed certificate, is it admissible?
A: Yes, if the computer was used regularly, fed information in the ordinary course, operating properly, and a certificate identifying the record and describing its production is submitted, it is admissible. [Source: Section 63, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admissibility of electronic records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 63: Admissibility of electronic records

Q: Under sub-section (4), what specific document must accompany an electronic record every time it is submitted for admission?
A: A certificate identifying the record, describing its production, giving device particulars, dealing with sub-section (2) conditions, and purporting to be signed by a person in charge or an expert must be submitted. [Source: Section 63, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admissibility of electronic records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 63: Admissibility of electronic records

Q: If a computer was broken for a week during a three-year period, does that automatically make all its outputs inadmissible?
A: No, sub-section (2)(c) allows admissibility if the period the computer was out of operation 'was not such as to affect the electronic record or the accuracy of its contents.' [Source: Section 63, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admissibility of electronic records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 63: Admissibility of electronic records

Q: What is the legal effect of submitting the required certificate signed by the person in charge under sub-section (4)?
A: The certificate shall be evidence of any matter stated within it, fulfilling the evidentiary requirement to admit the electronic record without calling the person to testify to those technical facts directly. [Source: Section 63, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admissibility of electronic records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 64: Rules as to notice to produce

Q: Before presenting secondary evidence of a document held by the opposing party, what procedural step must generally be taken?
A: The party proposing to give secondary evidence must previously give the party in possession of the document (or their advocate) a notice to produce it, as prescribed by law or as the Court considers reasonable. [Source: Section 64, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Rules as to notice to produce

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 64: Rules as to notice to produce

Q: What rule does Section 64 of BSA 2023 set for giving secondary evidence of a document held by an adversary?
A: Section 64 of BSA 2023 requires that a notice to produce the original must be given to the adverse party before secondary evidence can be admitted, though it lists several exceptions where notice is dispensed with. [Source: Section 64, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Rules as to notice to produce

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 64: Rules as to notice to produce

Q: If A wants to use a photocopy of a letter that B currently possesses, but A knows B obtained the original letter by fraud, does A have to give B notice to produce it?
A: No, the proviso (c) states that notice shall not be required when it appears or is proved that the adverse party has obtained possession of the original by fraud or force. [Source: Section 64, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Rules as to notice to produce

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 64: Rules as to notice to produce

Q: Who are the two specific people a 'notice to produce' can legally be given to under this section?
A: The notice can be given to the party in whose possession or power the document is, or to his advocate or representative. [Source: Section 64, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Rules as to notice to produce

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 64: Rules as to notice to produce

Q: Is notice required if the document the party wants to prove is itself a notice?
A: No, proviso (a) explicitly states that such notice shall not be required when the document to be proved is itself a notice. [Source: Section 64, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Rules as to notice to produce

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 64: Rules as to notice to produce

Q: What happens if a party attempts to submit secondary evidence of an opponent's document without having given the required notice (and no exceptions apply)?
A: The secondary evidence 'shall not be given' and will be deemed inadmissible by the Court. [Source: Section 64, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Rules as to notice to produce

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 65: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

Q: If a contract is submitted and it is claimed that a specific person signed it, what must be done regarding that signature?
A: If a document is alleged to be signed or written by any person, the signature or the handwriting of so much of the document as is alleged to be in that person's handwriting must be proved to be in his handwriting. [Source: Section 65, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 65: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

Q: What does Section 65 of BSA 2023 require when a document's authorship is alleged?
A: Section 65 of BSA 2023 requires that the specific signature or handwriting on a document alleged to be of a particular person must actually be proved to be in their handwriting. [Source: Section 65, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 65: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

Q: If a plaintiff produces a hand-written will and claims the deceased wrote paragraph 3 and signed it, what specifically must the plaintiff prove?
A: They must prove that the handwriting of paragraph 3, and the signature itself, are in the deceased person's handwriting. [Source: Section 65, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 65: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

Q: What two specific physical elements of a document does this section explicitly mention as needing proof of authorship?
A: The section explicitly mentions the 'signature' and the 'handwriting.' [Source: Section 65, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 65: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

Q: If only one paragraph of a ten-page printed document is alleged to have been handwritten by the defendant, must the plaintiff prove the defendant wrote the whole document?
A: No, they only must prove the handwriting of 'so much of the document as is alleged to be in that person's handwriting.' [Source: Section 65, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 65: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

Q: What happens if a party submits a signed letter but fails to provide any proof that the signature actually belongs to the alleged author?
A: The document will likely not be accepted as having been authored by that person, because the statutory requirement to prove the handwriting has not been met. [Source: Section 65, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of signature and handwriting of person alleged to have signed or written document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 66: Proof as to electronic signature

Q: If a document has an electronic signature, does the party submitting it need to prove who made that signature?
A: Yes, if the electronic signature of any subscriber is alleged to have been affixed to an electronic record, the fact that it is their signature must be proved, except in the case of a secure electronic signature. [Source: Section 66, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to electronic signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 66: Proof as to electronic signature

Q: What does Section 66 of BSA 2023 state about electronic signatures?
A: Section 66 of BSA 2023 states that the fact an electronic signature belongs to a specific subscriber must be proved, unless it is a secure electronic signature. [Source: Section 66, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to electronic signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 66: Proof as to electronic signature

Q: A bank submits a loan agreement with a standard (non-secure) electronic signature belonging to a customer. Do they have to prove the customer actually signed it?
A: Yes, because except in the case of a secure electronic signature, the fact that such electronic signature is the electronic signature of the subscriber must be proved. [Source: Section 66, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to electronic signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 66: Proof as to electronic signature

Q: What specific type of signature is exempted from the general requirement of proof under this section?
A: A 'secure electronic signature' is explicitly exempted from this requirement. [Source: Section 66, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to electronic signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 66: Proof as to electronic signature

Q: Is every single type of electronic signature subject to this burden of proof?
A: No, the section explicitly begins with the exception 'Except in the case of a secure electronic signature'. [Source: Section 66, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to electronic signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 66: Proof as to electronic signature

Q: What happens if a party submits an electronic record with a standard electronic signature but fails to prove it belongs to the alleged subscriber?
A: The electronic signature will likely not be legally attributed to that subscriber, rendering the document potentially invalid or unenforceable against them. [Source: Section 66, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to electronic signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 67: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

Q: If a law requires a document (like a will) to have witnesses, how must that document be proven in court?
A: It shall not be used as evidence until at least one attesting witness has been called to prove its execution, if an attesting witness is alive, subject to the Court's process, and capable of giving evidence. [Source: Section 67, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 67: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

Q: What is the primary rule established by Section 67 of BSA 2023 for attested documents?
A: Section 67 of BSA 2023 establishes that a document required by law to be attested cannot be used as evidence unless at least one capable attesting witness is called to prove its execution. [Source: Section 67, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 67: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

Q: If a will has two witnesses, and both are alive and capable, does the lawyer need to call both of them to testify?
A: No, the section only requires that 'one attesting witness at least has been called for the purpose of proving its execution.' [Source: Section 67, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 67: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

Q: What are the three conditions an attesting witness must meet for the requirement to call them to apply?
A: The witness must be alive, subject to the process of the Court, and capable of giving evidence. [Source: Section 67, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 67: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

Q: Is it always necessary to call an attesting witness for a registered sale deed if no one denies who signed it?
A: No, the proviso states it is not necessary to call an attesting witness for a document registered under the Indian Registration Act, 1908 (unless it's a will), unless its execution is specifically denied. [Source: Section 67, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 67: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

Q: What happens to a legally required attested document if the party trying to use it refuses to call the available attesting witness?
A: According to the section, 'it shall not be used as evidence' at all. [Source: Section 67, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of execution of document required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 68: Proof where no attesting witness found

Q: How can a legally required attested document be proven if all the witnesses who signed it have died or disappeared?
A: It must be proved that the attestation of at least one attesting witness is in their handwriting, and that the signature of the person executing the document is in that person's handwriting. [Source: Section 68, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof where no attesting witness found

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 68: Proof where no attesting witness found

Q: What procedure does Section 68 of BSA 2023 provide when attesting witnesses are unavailable?
A: Section 68 of BSA 2023 provides that if no attesting witness can be found, proof must be given of the handwriting of at least one attesting witness and of the person executing the document. [Source: Section 68, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof where no attesting witness found

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 68: Proof where no attesting witness found

Q: A 50-year-old will needs to be proven, but both witnesses are deceased. Can the will still be validated?
A: Yes, by proving that the attestation of at least one witness is in their handwriting, and the signature of the executor is in their handwriting. [Source: Section 68, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof where no attesting witness found

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 68: Proof where no attesting witness found

Q: What two specific things must be proven through handwriting analysis under this section?
A: First, the attestation of at least one attesting witness, and second, the signature of the person executing the document. [Source: Section 68, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof where no attesting witness found

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 68: Proof where no attesting witness found

Q: Does this section apply if an attesting witness is alive and available to testify?
A: No, this section specifically applies only 'If no such attesting witness can be found.' [Source: Section 68, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof where no attesting witness found

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 68: Proof where no attesting witness found

Q: What happens if the court accepts the handwriting proof under this section?
A: The document is legally proven as executed and attested, allowing it to be used as evidence despite the absence of live witness testimony. [Source: Section 68, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof where no attesting witness found

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 69: Admission of execution by party to attested document

Q: If a person admits they signed a legally required attested document, does a witness still need to be called to prove they signed it?
A: No, the admission of a party to an attested document of its execution by himself shall be sufficient proof of its execution as against him. [Source: Section 69, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admission of execution by party to attested document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 69: Admission of execution by party to attested document

Q: What rule does Section 69 of BSA 2023 establish regarding admissions?
A: Section 69 of BSA 2023 establishes that a party's own admission of executing an attested document is sufficient proof of its execution against that specific party. [Source: Section 69, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admission of execution by party to attested document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 69: Admission of execution by party to attested document

Q: If A signs a mortgage deed (which requires attestation) and later openly admits in court that they signed it, is the deed proven against A?
A: Yes, A's admission shall be sufficient proof of its execution as against him, even though it is a document required by law to be attested. [Source: Section 69, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admission of execution by party to attested document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 69: Admission of execution by party to attested document

Q: Against whom exactly is the admission of execution considered sufficient proof under this section?
A: The admission is sufficient proof of execution only 'as against him' (the party making the admission). [Source: Section 69, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admission of execution by party to attested document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 69: Admission of execution by party to attested document

Q: Does this section mean the document is fully proven against a third party who did not admit execution?
A: No, the section specifies the admission is sufficient proof 'as against him,' meaning the party who actually made the admission. [Source: Section 69, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admission of execution by party to attested document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 69: Admission of execution by party to attested document

Q: By making the admission sufficient proof, what procedural burden is lifted from the opposing party?
A: The opposing party is relieved of the burden of calling an attesting witness (under Section 67) to prove execution against the admitting party. [Source: Section 69, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Admission of execution by party to attested document

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 70: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

Q: What happens if the witness called to prove a document lies and says they never saw the person sign it?
A: If the attesting witness denies or does not recollect the execution of the document, its execution may be proved by other evidence. [Source: Section 70, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 70: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

Q: What does Section 70 of BSA 2023 permit if an attesting witness fails to confirm execution?
A: Section 70 of BSA 2023 permits the execution of the document to be proved by other evidence if the attesting witness denies or does not recollect the execution. [Source: Section 70, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 70: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

Q: A witness to a will testifies that they were drunk and cannot remember if the testator actually signed the document in front of them. Is the will automatically void?
A: No, because if the attesting witness does not recollect the execution, its execution may be proved by other evidence. [Source: Section 70, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 70: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

Q: What two specific actions or states of mind of the attesting witness trigger the application of this section?
A: The section is triggered if the attesting witness either 'denies' or 'does not recollect' the execution of the document. [Source: Section 70, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 70: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

Q: Is the party relying on the document blocked from using handwriting experts if the primary witness turns hostile?
A: No, this section explicitly provides an exception, allowing the party to use 'other evidence' (like handwriting experts) to prove execution. [Source: Section 70, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 70: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

Q: What legal safeguard does this section provide for parties relying on attested documents?
A: It safeguards the document from being invalidated solely because an attesting witness turns hostile, becomes uncooperative, or loses their memory. [Source: Section 70, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof when attesting witness denies execution

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 71: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

Q: If a document has witness signatures on it, but the law doesn't actually require it to be witnessed, how is it proven?
A: An attested document not required by law to be attested may be proved as if it was unattested. [Source: Section 71, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 71: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

Q: What rule does Section 71 of BSA 2023 establish regarding unnecessary attestation?
A: Section 71 of BSA 2023 establishes that if a document is attested but not required by law to be attested, it may be proved as if it was unattested. [Source: Section 71, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 71: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

Q: A person writes a simple IOU note to a friend and has a neighbor sign as a witness, even though IOUs don't legally need witnesses. Must the neighbor be called to testify?
A: No, because an attested document not required by law to be attested may be proved as if it was unattested. [Source: Section 71, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 71: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

Q: What specific legal condition must be true about the document for this section to apply?
A: The document must be 'not required by law to be attested.' [Source: Section 71, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 71: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

Q: Does this section apply to a will that legally requires attestation, but the party wants to prove it without calling the witnesses?
A: No, the section explicitly only applies to a document 'not required by law to be attested.' [Source: Section 71, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 71: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

Q: What is the procedural benefit of this section for a party trying to prove an over-formalized document?
A: The party is saved the burden and expense of tracking down and calling attesting witnesses (under Section 67) when the law never required them in the first place. [Source: Section 71, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of document not required by law to be attested

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 72: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

Q: Can a judge compare a disputed signature against a known, genuine signature to see if they match?
A: Yes, to ascertain if a signature is genuine, any signature admitted or proved to the Court's satisfaction to be by that person may be compared with the disputed one. [Source: Section 72, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 72: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

Q: What power does Section 72 of BSA 2023 give the Court regarding handwriting and signatures?
A: Section 72 of BSA 2023 gives the Court the power to compare disputed signatures, writings, or seals with proven ones, and to direct anyone present to write words for comparison. [Source: Section 72, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 72: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

Q: A defendant denies writing a threatening letter. Can the judge order the defendant to write out the same words in the courtroom right then and there?
A: Yes, the Court may direct any person present in Court to write any words or figures for the purpose of enabling the Court to compare the writings. [Source: Section 72, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 72: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

Q: Under sub-section (1), what must be true about the 'comparison' signature before the Court can use it to evaluate the disputed signature?
A: The comparison signature must be 'admitted or proved to the satisfaction of the Court to have been written or made by that person.' [Source: Section 72, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 72: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

Q: Can a proven signature only be used for comparison if it was originally submitted as evidence for some other part of the case?
A: No, it may be compared with the disputed one 'although that signature, writing or seal has not been produced or proved for any other purpose.' [Source: Section 72, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 72: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

Q: What is the legal scope of this section beyond just handwriting and physical seals?
A: Sub-section (3) dictates that this section applies also, with any necessary modifications, to finger impressions. [Source: Section 72, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Comparison of signature, writing or seal with others admitted or proved

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 73: Proof as to verification of digital signature

Q: How can a court verify that a digital signature actually belongs to the person who supposedly used it?
A: The Court may direct the person, Controller, or Certifying Authority to produce the Digital Signature Certificate, or direct anyone to apply the public key to verify it. [Source: Section 73, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to verification of digital signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 73: Proof as to verification of digital signature

Q: What procedures does Section 73 of BSA 2023 outline for verifying digital signatures?
A: Section 73 of BSA 2023 outlines that the Court may direct the production of the Digital Signature Certificate or direct the application of the public key to verify the signature. [Source: Section 73, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to verification of digital signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 73: Proof as to verification of digital signature

Q: A plaintiff claims the defendant digitally signed a contract, but the defendant denies it. Can the court force the Certifying Authority to hand over the certificate details?
A: Yes, the Court may direct that person or the Controller or the Certifying Authority to produce the Digital Signature Certificate. [Source: Section 73, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to verification of digital signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 73: Proof as to verification of digital signature

Q: What specific technical component is used by a person under clause (b) to verify a digital signature?
A: The person must apply the 'public key listed in the Digital Signature Certificate' to verify the signature. [Source: Section 73, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to verification of digital signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 73: Proof as to verification of digital signature

Q: Is the Court limited to only asking the alleged signer themselves to produce the certificate?
A: No, clause (a) allows the Court to direct 'that person or the Controller or the Certifying Authority' to produce it. [Source: Section 73, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to verification of digital signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 73: Proof as to verification of digital signature

Q: What is the legal objective of applying the public key under this section?
A: The objective is to ascertain whether a digital signature is that of the person by whom it purports to have been affixed. [Source: Section 73, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof as to verification of digital signature

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 74: Public and private documents

Q: Are court judgments and official government records considered a special category of documents?
A: Yes, documents forming the acts or records of acts of the sovereign authority, official bodies, tribunals, and public officers are classified as public documents. [Source: Section 74, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public and private documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 74: Public and private documents

Q: How does Section 74 of BSA 2023 classify documents?
A: Section 74 of BSA 2023 classifies documents into two exhaustive categories: public documents (official sovereign, legislative, judicial, executive records) and private documents (all others). [Source: Section 74, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public and private documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 74: Public and private documents

Q: If a person registers their private house sale deed with the state registry office, does the record kept by the State become a public document?
A: Yes, under sub-section (1)(b), public records kept in any State or Union territory of private documents are public documents. [Source: Section 74, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public and private documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 74: Public and private documents

Q: What are the three branches of public officers (Indian or foreign) whose acts or records are considered public documents?
A: The three branches are legislative, judicial, and executive. [Source: Section 74, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public and private documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 74: Public and private documents

Q: Is a letter written between two private business partners regarding a commercial deal a public document?
A: No, sub-section (2) explicitly states that all other documents except those referred to in sub-section (1) are private documents. [Source: Section 74, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public and private documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 74: Public and private documents

Q: What is the underlying legal distinction created by dividing all documents into these two specific categories?
A: The distinction dictates how the documents are treated in court, specifically regarding the right to inspect them and the ability to prove them using certified copies (as detailed in subsequent sections). [Source: Section 74, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Public and private documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 75: Certified copies of public documents

Q: If a citizen needs an official copy of a public document for a court case, how do they get it?
A: Every public officer having custody of a public document which any person has a right to inspect must give that person a copy on demand and payment of legal fees, along with a signed and dated certificate. [Source: Section 75, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Certified copies of public documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 75: Certified copies of public documents

Q: What duty does Section 75 of BSA 2023 impose on public officers regarding public documents?
A: Section 75 of BSA 2023 imposes a duty on public officers to provide, on demand and payment, certified true copies of public documents to any person who has a right to inspect them. [Source: Section 75, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Certified copies of public documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 75: Certified copies of public documents

Q: A citizen pays the fee and asks a court clerk for a copy of a judgment. The clerk just hands them a plain photocopy. Is this a valid certified copy?
A: No, it must include a certificate written at the foot stating it is a true copy, dated, subscribed with the officer's name and title, and sealed if they are authorized to use a seal. [Source: Section 75, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Certified copies of public documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 75: Certified copies of public documents

Q: What specific physical elements must the officer append to the copy to make it a legally valid 'certified copy'?
A: A certificate declaring it a true copy, the date, the officer's signature (name), their official title, and a seal (if authorized). [Source: Section 75, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Certified copies of public documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 75: Certified copies of public documents

Q: Can a citizen demand a certified copy of a highly classified public document they have no legal right to see?
A: No, the section restricts the duty to provide copies only to a 'public document, which any person has a right to inspect.' [Source: Section 75, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Certified copies of public documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 75: Certified copies of public documents

Q: How does the Explanation define who has 'custody' of these documents?
A: Any officer who, by the ordinary course of official duty, is authorized to deliver such copies, is legally deemed to have the custody of such documents. [Source: Section 75, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Certified copies of public documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 76: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

Q: How can you legally prove what a public document says without bringing the original into court?
A: Certified copies may be produced in proof of the contents of the public documents or parts of the public documents of which they purport to be copies. [Source: Section 76, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 76: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

Q: What does Section 76 of BSA 2023 allow regarding public documents?
A: Section 76 of BSA 2023 allows the production of certified copies to prove the contents of public documents or parts thereof. [Source: Section 76, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 76: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

Q: If a lawyer obtains a valid certified copy of a birth certificate from the government registry, can they use it in court to prove the child's birth date?
A: Yes, because certified copies may be produced in proof of the contents of the public documents of which they purport to be copies. [Source: Section 76, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 76: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

Q: What specific type of document is this rule exclusively designed to prove?
A: The rule is exclusively designed to prove the contents of 'public documents.' [Source: Section 76, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 76: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

Q: Does this section allow proving a private document by producing a certified copy of it?
A: No, the section specifically refers to 'proof of the contents of the public documents.' [Source: Section 76, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 76: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

Q: What legal burden is lifted from a party by this rule?
A: The party is relieved from the burden of subpoenaing original public records and the government officials who keep them, streamlining the presentation of evidence. [Source: Section 76, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of documents by production of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 77: Proof of other official documents

Q: How can the proceedings of Parliament be proven in a court of law?
A: The proceedings of Parliament may be proved by the journals of those bodies, by published Acts or abstracts, or by copies purporting to be printed by order of the Government concerned. [Source: Section 77, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of other official documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 77: Proof of other official documents

Q: What does Section 77 of BSA 2023 specify?
A: Section 77 of BSA 2023 specifies the exact methods by which various classes of official public documents, such as government acts, parliamentary proceedings, and foreign public documents, may be proved. [Source: Section 77, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of other official documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 77: Proof of other official documents

Q: If a party needs to prove an order issued by the President of India, how can they do it?
A: They can prove it by producing copies or extracts contained in the Official Gazette. [Source: Section 77, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of other official documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 77: Proof of other official documents

Q: Under clause (f), what two specific certifications are required to prove a public document of a foreign country using a copy?
A: The copy must be certified by the legal keeper thereof, and it must have a certificate under the seal of a Notary Public, Indian Consul, or diplomatic agent verifying the legal custody. [Source: Section 77, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of other official documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 77: Proof of other official documents

Q: Can an act of the Central Government be proved by a simple oral statement from a government employee?
A: No, it must be proved by the records of the Departments certified by the head, or by a document purporting to be printed by order of the Government. [Source: Section 77, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of other official documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 77: Proof of other official documents

Q: What is the evidentiary value of a printed book purporting to be published by the authority of a municipal body?
A: Under clause (e), that printed book is legally accepted as proof of the proceedings of that municipal or local body. [Source: Section 77, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Proof of other official documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 78: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

Q: Does a judge automatically assume a government-certified copy of a document is real, or must the person submitting it prove it isn't forged?
A: The Court shall presume to be genuine every document purporting to be a certificate or certified copy declared admissible by law and duly certified by a government officer. [Source: Section 78, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 78: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

Q: What legal presumption is established by Section 78 of BSA 2023?
A: Section 78 of BSA 2023 establishes a mandatory presumption that certified copies duly certified by government officers are genuine, provided they are in the substantially correct form. [Source: Section 78, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 78: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

Q: If a lawyer submits a state-certified copy of a land deed that looks completely proper, can the judge refuse to admit it on the suspicion that the officer's signature might be fake?
A: No, the Court 'shall presume' the document to be genuine and that the officer signing it held the official character they claim, unless proven otherwise. [Source: Section 78, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 78: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

Q: What specific condition must the document meet according to the proviso for this presumption to apply?
A: The document must be 'substantially in the form and purports to be executed in the manner directed by law in that behalf.' [Source: Section 78, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 78: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

Q: If a private citizen signs a 'certified copy' of their own diary, does the court presume it is genuine under this section?
A: No, the presumption only applies to documents purporting to be duly certified by 'any officer of the Central Government or of a State Government.' [Source: Section 78, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 78: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

Q: What is the practical effect of sub-section (2) regarding the officer who signed the document?
A: The party submitting the document does not have to independently prove that the person who signed the certificate actually held that official job title at the time they signed it. [Source: Section 78, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to genuineness of certified copies

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 79: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

Q: When a transcript of a witness's testimony from a previous trial is presented, does the court assume the transcript is accurate?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume that the document is genuine, that statements about the circumstances under which it was taken are true, and that the evidence was duly taken. [Source: Section 79, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 79: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

Q: What does Section 79 of BSA 2023 direct courts to presume regarding records of evidence and confessions?
A: Section 79 of BSA 2023 directs courts to presume that records of evidence or confessions signed by a Judge or Magistrate are genuine and were duly taken in accordance with law. [Source: Section 79, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 79: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

Q: A magistrate produces a written confession signed by an accused person. Does the prosecutor have to prove that the magistrate followed all procedural rules while taking it?
A: No, because the Court shall presume that such statement or confession was 'duly taken' and the statements about the circumstances of its taking are true. [Source: Section 79, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 79: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

Q: Who must purport to have signed the record of evidence or confession for this presumption to apply?
A: It must purport to be signed by any Judge or Magistrate, or by any officer authorized by law to take such evidence. [Source: Section 79, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 79: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

Q: Does this presumption apply to a written confession taken down and signed only by a private citizen?
A: No, it only applies to documents purporting to be signed by a 'Judge or Magistrate, or by any such officer as aforesaid.' [Source: Section 79, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 79: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

Q: How does this section facilitate the progress of trials involving past statements?
A: It prevents trials from getting bogged down in 'trials within trials' to prove the authenticity and procedural correctness of every piece of recorded court testimony or confession. [Source: Section 79, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence, etc

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 80: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

Q: If someone submits a copy of a daily newspaper to prove a public announcement was made, does the court automatically assume the newspaper is genuine?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume the genuineness of every document purporting to be a newspaper or journal, provided it is produced from proper custody. [Source: Section 80, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 80: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

Q: What documents does Section 80 of BSA 2023 require the court to presume are genuine?
A: Section 80 of BSA 2023 requires the court to presume the genuineness of Official Gazettes, newspapers, journals, and documents directed by law to be kept by a person, if produced from proper custody. [Source: Section 80, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 80: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

Q: A lawyer produces a 10-year-old Official Gazette found in a government archive. Will the court presume it is genuine?
A: Yes, because it purports to be the Official Gazette and is produced from the government archive, which constitutes 'proper custody.' [Source: Section 80, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 80: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

Q: According to the Explanation, what defines 'proper custody' for a document?
A: A document is in proper custody if it is in the place in which, and looked after by the person with whom, such document is required to be kept. [Source: Section 80, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 80: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

Q: Can a newspaper clipping found randomly on the street be presumed genuine under this section?
A: No, because the presumption requires that the document is 'produced from proper custody,' and finding it on the street does not meet that standard. [Source: Section 80, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 80: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

Q: If custody is technically improper, but the document is proven to have had a legitimate origin, what is the legal result?
A: The Explanation dictates that 'no custody is improper if it is proved to have had a legitimate origin,' meaning the presumption of genuineness will still apply. [Source: Section 80, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes, newspapers, and other documents

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 81: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

Q: Does the legal presumption of genuineness apply to digital versions of the Official Gazette?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume the genuineness of every electronic or digital record purporting to be the Official Gazette, if kept substantially in the required form and produced from proper custody. [Source: Section 81, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 81: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

Q: What does Section 81 of BSA 2023 extend the presumption of genuineness to?
A: Section 81 of BSA 2023 extends the presumption of genuineness to electronic or digital records purporting to be the Official Gazette or other legally required digital records. [Source: Section 81, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 81: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

Q: If a lawyer downloads the Official Gazette from the official government website and produces it in court, will the court presume it is genuine?
A: Yes, because it purports to be the Official Gazette in digital form and the official website constitutes proper custody. [Source: Section 81, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 81: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

Q: What two specific conditions must an electronic Gazette meet to trigger the presumption of genuineness?
A: It must be kept 'substantially in the form required by law' and 'produced from proper custody.' [Source: Section 81, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 81: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

Q: Does this section apply to a printed, paper copy of a daily newspaper?
A: No, this specific section only covers 'every electronic or digital record purporting to be the Official Gazette' or legally required digital records (Section 80 covers printed newspapers). [Source: Section 81, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 81: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

Q: What legal flexibility does the Explanation provide regarding the 'proper custody' of electronic records?
A: It provides that no custody is improper if it is proved to have had a legitimate origin, or if the circumstances of the case render that origin probable. [Source: Section 81, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Gazettes in electronic or digital record

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 82: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

Q: Are official government maps automatically considered accurate by the court?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume that maps or plans purporting to be made by the authority of the Central Government or any State Government were so made, and are accurate. [Source: Section 82, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 82: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

Q: What distinction does Section 82 of BSA 2023 draw between different types of maps?
A: Section 82 of BSA 2023 draws a distinction between government-authorized maps, which are presumed accurate, and maps made specifically for a legal case, which must be proved to be accurate. [Source: Section 82, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 82: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

Q: A plaintiff submits a national survey map to show property boundaries, and a separate sketch they hired a surveyor to draw specifically for the lawsuit. How does the court treat them differently?
A: The court presumes the national survey map is accurate, but the plaintiff must actively prove the hired surveyor's sketch is accurate. [Source: Section 82, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 82: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

Q: Whose specific authority must a map purport to be made under for the presumption of accuracy to apply?
A: It must purport to be made by the authority of the Central Government or any State Government. [Source: Section 82, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 82: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

Q: If a map is created by the government, but it was created specifically for the purpose of a particular court case, is it presumed accurate?
A: No, the section explicitly states 'but maps or plans made for the purposes of any cause must be proved to be accurate.' [Source: Section 82, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 82: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

Q: By granting this presumption to government maps, what time-consuming process is avoided during property or border disputes?
A: It avoids the need to call the original government cartographers or surveyors to testify and prove the accuracy of standard official maps in every single case. [Source: Section 82, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to maps or plans made by authority of Government

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 83: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

Q: When a lawyer cites a published book containing foreign laws or court judgments, does the judge assume the book is genuine?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume the genuineness of every book purporting to be published under government authority containing laws, and every book containing reports of court decisions. [Source: Section 83, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 83: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

Q: What presumption does Section 83 of BSA 2023 create regarding legal publications?
A: Section 83 of BSA 2023 creates a presumption that published books containing a country's laws (under government authority) or reports of its court decisions are genuine. [Source: Section 83, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 83: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

Q: If a party in an Indian court submits a printed book titled 'Supreme Court Cases' containing rulings from the US Supreme Court, will the Indian court presume the book is genuine?
A: Yes, because the court shall presume the genuineness of every book purporting to contain reports of decisions of the Courts of such country. [Source: Section 83, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 83: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

Q: For a book of laws to be presumed genuine under this section, whose authority must it purport to be printed or published under?
A: It must purport to be printed or published 'under the authority of the Government of any country.' [Source: Section 83, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 83: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

Q: Does a book of court decision reports need to explicitly claim it was published by the government to be presumed genuine?
A: No, the section applies the presumption to 'every book purporting to contain reports of decisions of the Courts of such country' without the 'government authority' requirement attached to law books. [Source: Section 83, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 83: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

Q: How does this section assist judges in handling cases involving foreign jurisdictions?
A: It allows judges to accept standard foreign law books and case reporters at face value without requiring diplomatic certification or expert testimony just to prove the book itself isn't a forgery. [Source: Section 83, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to collections of laws and reports of decisions

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 84: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

Q: If a person presents a power-of-attorney document stamped by a Notary Public, does the court assume it is legally valid?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume that a power-of-attorney executed before and authenticated by a Notary Public or specific officials was legally executed and authenticated. [Source: Section 84, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 84: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

Q: What does Section 84 of BSA 2023 instruct the Court to presume about powers-of-attorney?
A: Section 84 of BSA 2023 instructs the Court to presume that a power-of-attorney authenticated by recognized officials like a Notary Public, Judge, or Magistrate was properly executed and authenticated. [Source: Section 84, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 84: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

Q: An agent tries to sell land using a power-of-attorney signed only by the landowner and two private witnesses. Will the court automatically presume it was properly executed?
A: No, because the presumption only applies to documents executed before and authenticated by specific officials like a Notary Public or Magistrate. [Source: Section 84, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 84: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

Q: Name three specific types of officials listed in the section who can authenticate a power-of-attorney to trigger this presumption.
A: The officials include a Notary Public, any Court, Judge, Magistrate, Indian Consul or Vice-Consul, or representative of the Central Government. [Source: Section 84, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 84: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

Q: Does this presumption apply to a standard commercial contract authenticated by a notary?
A: No, the specific presumption in this section applies only to 'every document purporting to be a power-of-attorney.' [Source: Section 84, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 84: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

Q: By establishing this presumption, what evidentiary shortcut is provided to agents acting under a formal power-of-attorney?
A: Agents do not need to bring the principal (the person who gave them the power) into court to testify that they actually signed the document, saving significant time and effort. [Source: Section 84, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to powers-of-attorney

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 85: Presumption as to electronic agreements

Q: When an electronic contract contains the digital signatures of the parties, what does the law assume about how it was finalized?
A: The Court shall presume that the electronic record purporting to be an agreement was concluded by affixing the electronic or digital signature of the parties. [Source: Section 85, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic agreements

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 85: Presumption as to electronic agreements

Q: What presumption does Section 85 of BSA 2023 establish for digital contracts?
A: Section 85 of BSA 2023 establishes the presumption that an electronic agreement containing the parties' digital signatures was genuinely concluded by the affixing of those signatures. [Source: Section 85, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic agreements

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 85: Presumption as to electronic agreements

Q: A vendor sues a client over an unpaid digital invoice. The vendor presents an electronic agreement with the client's digital signature on it. What does the judge presume?
A: The judge shall presume that the agreement was formally concluded by the parties affixing their digital signatures. [Source: Section 85, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic agreements

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 85: Presumption as to electronic agreements

Q: What specific technological feature must the electronic record contain for this presumption to apply?
A: It must contain the 'electronic or digital signature of the parties.' [Source: Section 85, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic agreements

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 85: Presumption as to electronic agreements

Q: If a digital contract only has the typed name of one party at the bottom, without an actual electronic or digital signature, does this presumption apply?
A: No, the presumption strictly requires the document to contain the 'electronic or digital signature' of the parties. [Source: Section 85, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic agreements

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 85: Presumption as to electronic agreements

Q: How does this presumption align digital commerce with traditional contract law?
A: It grants digitally signed agreements the same initial evidentiary weight and presumption of finality as traditional paper contracts signed in ink. [Source: Section 85, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic agreements

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 86: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

Q: Does the law assume a digitally secured document has not been tampered with?
A: Yes, in any proceeding involving a secure electronic record, the Court shall presume unless the contrary is proved, that it has not been altered since the specific point of time to which the secure status relates. [Source: Section 86, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 86: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

Q: What does Section 86 of BSA 2023 presume about secure electronic signatures?
A: Section 86 of BSA 2023 presumes that a secure electronic signature is affixed by the subscriber with the intention of signing or approving the electronic record, unless proved otherwise. [Source: Section 86, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 86: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

Q: A bank submits a secure electronic record of a transaction. The defendant claims the bank altered the amount later. Who has the burden of proof?
A: The defendant has the burden of proof, because the Court shall presume the secure electronic record has not been altered unless the contrary is proved. [Source: Section 86, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 86: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

Q: What specific word describes the type of electronic record and signature that benefits from the presumptions in this section?
A: The specific word is 'secure' (secure electronic record, secure electronic signature). [Source: Section 86, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 86: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

Q: If an electronic record is NOT 'secure,' does the court still presume its authenticity and integrity under this section?
A: No, clause (2)(b) explicitly states that except in the case of a secure electronic record or signature, nothing in this section shall create any presumption relating to authenticity and integrity. [Source: Section 86, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 86: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

Q: What legal intention is automatically attributed to a subscriber who affixes a secure electronic signature?
A: The law presumes the signature was affixed 'with the intention of signing or approving the electronic record.' [Source: Section 86, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to electronic records and electronic signatures

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 87: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

Q: When an Electronic Signature Certificate is accepted by a user, does the court assume the details inside it are accurate?
A: Yes, the Court shall presume, unless the contrary is proved, that the information listed in the certificate is correct, except for unverified subscriber information. [Source: Section 87, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 87: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

Q: What presumption does Section 87 of BSA 2023 establish for Electronic Signature Certificates?
A: Section 87 of BSA 2023 establishes the presumption that information in an accepted Electronic Signature Certificate is correct, excluding any subscriber information specified as unverified. [Source: Section 87, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 87: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

Q: A digital certificate states it was issued to 'Company X' but includes an unverified phone number provided by the applicant. Will the court presume the phone number is correct?
A: No, the presumption of correctness applies 'except for information specified as subscriber information which has not been verified.' [Source: Section 87, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 87: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

Q: What action must the subscriber have taken regarding the certificate for this presumption to apply?
A: The certificate must have been 'accepted by the subscriber.' [Source: Section 87, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 87: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

Q: Is the presumption under this section absolute and final?
A: No, it is a rebuttable presumption, as the section states the Court shall presume it 'unless contrary is proved.' [Source: Section 87, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 87: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

Q: By establishing this presumption, what technical verification process is validated for courtroom use?
A: The technical verification process performed by the Certifying Authority when issuing the certificate is legally validated, shifting the burden to anyone challenging the certificate's details. [Source: Section 87, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to Electronic Signature Certificates

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 88: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

Q: If a party wants to submit a court judgment from another country, how does the Indian court know the copy is genuine?
A: The Court may presume it is genuine and accurate if it purports to be certified in a manner confirmed by an Indian Central Government representative as the manner commonly used in that foreign country. [Source: Section 88, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 88: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

Q: What does Section 88 of BSA 2023 allow the court to presume about foreign judicial records?
A: Section 88 of BSA 2023 allows the court to presume that certified copies of foreign judicial records are genuine and accurate if certified in the customary manner of that country, as verified by an Indian representative. [Source: Section 88, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 88: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

Q: A plaintiff submits a French court decree, certified by a French court clerk, and attaches a letter from the Indian Consul in France confirming that this is how France certifies its decrees. Will the Indian court accept it?
A: Yes, the Court may presume the document is genuine and accurate based on that certification by the representative of the Central Government. [Source: Section 88, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 88: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

Q: Under sub-section (2), what specific official title is deemed to be a 'representative of the Central Government' for this section?
A: A 'Political Agent' as defined in the General Clauses Act, 1897, is deemed to be a representative of the Central Government. [Source: Section 88, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 88: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

Q: Is the court completely forced to accept a foreign judicial record just because it has the correct stamps?
A: No, the section states the Court 'may presume' it is genuine, making it a discretionary presumption rather than a mandatory 'shall presume.' [Source: Section 88, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 88: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

Q: What legal hurdle does this section eliminate for parties involved in transnational disputes?
A: It eliminates the need to bring foreign court officials to India to testify about the authenticity of their own legal records. [Source: Section 88, BSA 2023]

metadata.section_title: Presumption as to certified copies of foreign judicial records

content:
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA) - Section 89: Presumption as to books, maps and charts

Q: Can a judge look at a published atlas to confirm the location of a town without requiring the publisher to testify?
